description:
Publish source as an app: a process Valet builds from your files and runs behind its own URL. Use it when the user wants an app on Valet that needs a server, a background process, or a database. A Procfile at the root says how to start each process type; the web type serves the app's URL and must listen on $PORT, which Valet sets. Node, Python, and Go are supported. The organization's release policies check each publish on Valet's side; a publish that does not meet one is refused or returns an evaluation, and the answer names what to fix.

With files, Valet writes the app's valet.yaml from title and description. files carries text only: source, Procfile, configuration, and a manifest the build installs from (package.json, requirements.txt, or go.mod), never installed packages. When you can run git with network access, or the app is large or holds binary files, call create_push, push, and pass push: {id, commit} instead; the commit supplies its own valet.yaml. Pass files or push, not both.

Create the app first with create_service (kind: app), then publish to its name. Publishing replaces the app's source, so read get_source first when the app is not yours. Returns a build id: poll get_build every ten to fifteen seconds until deploy_state is up, crashed, or refused, and between polls tell the person what its phase says the build is doing. A crashed release leaves the last one serving, so a working URL does not prove the new release is live; a crashed process's state_reason says what to fix.

Write the app to start without its variables and resources and serve a page saying what is missing, never exiting. Then attach_resource, which takes the app's own variables too, applies both in one restart; set_env_vars restarts it with variables alone. A new app is private: only members of the organization that owns it can open it, after signing in to Valet. Use set_service_access to make it public or password-protected. Requires connecting a Valet account.

description.description: With files, a call without it is refused. One sentence saying what the app does, for a person deciding whether to open it.

discard_draft.description: Set true to discard an open draft on this app that another session left. Omit to be told about it instead. Not used with push.

files.description: The app's files. Give this or push, not both. A Procfile at the root is required.

path.description: Path relative to the app root, with '/' separators and no leading slash. It may not contain '.' or '..' segments.

idempotency_key.description: An opaque key of your choosing. Repeating a call with the same key returns the first call's result instead of starting a second build. Use a new key for new files: a repeated key returns the earlier result even when the files changed.

name.description: The app's name, which is the first label of its URL. The app must exist: create it first with create_service. Publishing to it replaces its source.

org_name.description: The Valet organization to publish into. Omit to use the organization the account joined first.

push.description: Publish a Git push instead of files: the id create_push returned and the commit you pushed to its branch. Use it when you can run git with network access, because it sends only what changed. Pass files or push, not both; every other argument keeps its meaning.

commit.description: The full sha of the commit you pushed to the push's branch. The recipe create_push returned prints it.

title.description: With files, a call without it is refused. What the app is called, written for a person. It labels the app wherever it is listed.

name: publish_app

build_id.description: ID of the build the publish started. Pass it to get_build and poll until deploy_state is up, crashed, or refused. Absent when no build started.

name.description: Name of the app. It is the first label of its URL.

no_changes.description: True when the pushed tree is what the app already runs, so no build started. Absent otherwise.

org.description: Name of the Valet organization the call acted in.

url.description: URL that serves the app. Absent while the app has no route.

title: Publish an app
